name: improve
description: Use your most capable model to audit your codebase and write plans for cheaper models to execute.
one_liner: A tool that has a top-tier AI inspect your entire codebase, find the messy or risky parts, and write step-by-step fix-it instructions that a cheaper AI (or a junior developer) can follow without getting lost.
buyer: A startup CTO or engineering lead who has accumulated technical debt and wants a prioritized, evidence-based cleanup list instead of guessing where to spend limited engineering time.
business_use_cases: A fractional CTO runs it against a client's inherited codebase as the first deliverable of an engagement, turning the findings into a priced cleanup roadmap.
An engineering manager uses the security/performance-focused audit modes to justify a tech-debt sprint to leadership with file:line evidence instead of opinions.
A dev agency uses `/improve execute` to cheaply implement the plans with a junior/cheap model while senior engineers only review diffs, cutting billable hours per fix.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a flat-fee 'codebase health audit' service for startups, powered by this tool
Retainer-based ongoing tech-debt management for client codebases

steal_this: Run `/improve quick` against three local startups' repos for free, turn the findings table into a one-page report, and pitch a paid full audit off the back of it.
